raw.description: The application does not implement any CSRF protection mechanisms, making it vulnerable to Cross-Site Request Forgery attacks.
raw.exploit: An attacker can trick a user into making unwanted requests to the server by exploiting the user's authenticated session.

raw.description: The application directly renders user input (URL) without proper sanitization or escaping, which can lead to Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerabilities.
raw.exploit: An attacker can inject malicious scripts into the URL input field, which will be executed in the context of the user's browser.

raw.description: The database password is hardcoded in the source code, which can lead to unauthorized access if the code is exposed.
raw.exploit: An attacker with access to the source code can use the hardcoded credentials to connect to the database and manipulate data.

raw.description: The application fetches URLs provided by the user without validation, making it vulnerable to Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF).
raw.exploit: An attacker can provide a URL pointing to internal services or sensitive endpoints, potentially gaining unauthorized access to internal systems.

raw.description: The application uses parameterized queries to prevent SQL injection, but there is no input validation on the URL parameter, which could lead to other injection attacks if not handled properly.
raw.exploit: While SQL injection is mitigated, an attacker could still attempt to exploit other types of injection vulnerabilities if input validation is not enforced.
